name: Bayraktar TB2

placement_rationale.text: 6 km represents where TB2 does its forward ISR/strike orbit near the line, not the runway-based airfield its ground control station actually operates from — a fixed-wing MALE UAV needing a runway is normally based well to the rear and reaches the front via satellite/line-of-sight relay, so the airfield itself sits far outside this band. 6 km falls inside doctrine.md §2's drone-dense corridor (~30 km either side of the front), consistent with this asset's own employment_notes, which describe reduced but still-present forward activity now that denser Russian IADS has pushed most of its work further from direct front-line contact than in the war's opening weeks. (Nudged 6→5.5 km from this category's shared round-number value so it doesn't literally coincide with side_a-uav-punisher, side_a-uav-switchblade-600 on the map's distance axis — a small, deterministic spread within the same band, not a new plausibility claim beyond what's already argued above.)

cost.display: ~$1-2M per system component (widely cited estimate, not officially disclosed)

characteristics: Strength: Combines long-endurance ISR with an organic strike capability in one airframe, unlike pure-recon or pure-strike drone types

Limitation: Vulnerable to modern integrated air defense at altitude and range once opposing SAM coverage is dense - effectiveness dropped sharply after the war's opening weeks as Russian air defense adapted
Estimated quantity available: Dozens in service; exact current total not disclosed
employment_notes: Iconic in the war's opening phase for strikes on armor and logistics columns; its reduced later-war effectiveness against a denser Russian IADS is itself a widely-cited lesson about air defense adaptation
contrast_vs_traditional: TB2 opened the war as the headline example of an armed medium-altitude UAV doing a job traditional airpower doctrine reserved for manned strike aircraft — find, track and strike a target without risking a pilot. Persistent short-range air defense has since pushed it out of contested airspace near the front, which is itself the doctrine.md finding in miniature: control of the lower sky, not a platform's own capability, sets where it can actually operate.

notes: Rests only on tertiary reference works; wants a primary or trade source.

altitude_band_m.note: Service ceiling 8,239 m; a documented endurance flight held 5,486 m. Published figures for this airframe.
